rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the eight-peak elution window and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. This provides a baseline for targeted changes in gradient slope, solvent window, and temperature.

Double the gradient duration at fixed solvent endpoints and temperature to distinguish slope-sensitive overlaps from persistent selectivity limitations. All eight peaks eluted early in the first run, leaving room to spread the crowded groups.
The shallower gradient resolved most overlaps but left one nearly coeluting pair. Raise temperature while holding the gradient fixed to test selectivity changes and gain additional time margin.

Test a slightly steeper gradient at 60 C to shift the remaining close pair away from its current overlap while shortening the run. Monitor the early cluster, whose smallest resolution of 1.61 leaves limited margin.

Use the 20-minute gradient to restore resolution in the early cluster, then lower temperature by 5 C to shift the remaining late overlap. The previous runs suggest enough time margin to keep the last peak below 10 minutes.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to adjust selectivity while slightly flattening the gradient relative to injection 4. This targets its marginal early overlap while testing whether the late pair retains sufficient resolution.

Use a narrower solvent window to obtain a slope between the tested settings, slightly shallower than injection 6. This should improve both early marginal pairs while preserving the late pair’s resolution, with all peaks still inside the gradient.

Injection 7 already achieves the maximum CRF and remains the benchmark. Raise phi0 one step to seek a shorter fully resolved separation, testing whether the shallower solvent span compensates for reduced initial retention.

Keep injection 7 as the maximum-score benchmark and test the low-temperature selectivity regime using its gradient. This explores whether a different elution order offers wider resolution margins for subsequent shortening.

Shorten the low-temperature gradient to test whether its remaining overlap improves with slope while bringing the last peak earlier. Injection 7 remains the maximum-CRF fallback if this compresses other pairs below baseline resolution.

The low-temperature close pair appears to approach an elution-order crossing as the gradient steepens; shorten another step to test separation on the other side. Watch the late pair, whose resolution was only 1.55 at eight minutes, while retaining injection 7 as the proven optimum-score method.

Raise temperature one step at the shorter gradient to test whether selectivity improves both remaining overlaps while further reducing retention. Injection 7 remains the established maximum-score method.

At 30 C, all but one pair are resolved with useful margins. Shorten the gradient to push the remaining overlap farther beyond its apparent slope-driven crossing and test a substantially faster separation, retaining injection 7 as the maximum-score benchmark.

Return to the successful high-temperature regime and slightly flatten injection 8’s gradient to improve its sole unresolved early pair. This tests whether a higher starting organic fraction can deliver full resolution sooner than injection 7 without sacrificing the late pair.

The high-temperature refinements expose opposing resolution constraints, so test intermediate-temperature selectivity using the proven gradient. This may separate the crowded groups through a different elution order while keeping the final peak below ten minutes; injection 7 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

Flatten the gradient at 45 C to test whether the single remaining overlap gains resolution while the late pair stays resolved. The current last peak at 8.06 minutes leaves some time margin, and injection 7 already secures the maximum CRF.

Refine the maximum-score method with a slightly steeper slope of 0.04583 organic fraction per minute versus 0.045 in injection 7. This should shorten retention slightly while testing the narrow resolution margin of the early cluster.

The close middle pair at 45 C barely responded to gradient duration, indicating a temperature-selectivity limitation. Test 40 C with a shorter gradient to seek a faster resolved elution pattern, while retaining injection 7 as the proven maximum-score method.

Test a higher starting organic fraction in the low-temperature regime to shift the persistent middle overlap and shorten retention. The narrower gradient span may preserve the late pair’s resolution; injection 7 remains the established maximum-score method.

Test whether a further increase in starting organic fraction moves the early cluster through an elution-order crossing and yields a faster resolved separation. The first peak should remain observable, and injection 7 remains the proven maximum-CRF method.

Test beyond the apparent early-pair crossing with a higher starting organic fraction and a shallower gradient to recover separation in the compressed cluster. This is a search for a faster alternative; injection 7 already secures the maximum possible CRF.

Return near injection 7 and test a slightly shallower gradient with a lower endpoint, targeting larger resolution margins in the early cluster. The late close pair may limit this adjustment, so retain injection 7 as the proven maximum-score method.

Test a gradient slope between injections 7 and 22 to refine the balance between early-cluster resolution and the late critical pair. Injection 7 already achieves the maximum CRF; this nearby setting tests whether that score extends to a slightly shallower gradient.

Lengthen injection 19’s gradient to improve its sole unresolved pair; the low-temperature runs show that this overlap improves with a shallower slope. The last peak is expected to remain below ten minutes, while injection 7 remains the established maximum-score method.

Slightly flatten injection 24’s gradient from 0.040 to 0.0375 organic fraction per minute to lift its sole marginal pair above R = 1.5, with the last peak expected below ten minutes. Injection 7 remains the proven maximum-score method and the faster fully resolved option.
